title: Stallioneer Bulk toggles, Options consolidation, and DNS cleanup checkpoint
content:
Stallioneer had another consolidation pass, with the work split between library workflow polish and platform reliability. The core direction is clearer now: Auth owns accounts, Options owns local library management, Inventory remains the main daily surface, and Bulk keeps shrinking into only the batch actions that still need a separate place.

What changed:

  • Bulk tag toggles: selecting books now fills a tag badge list. Clicking a badge immediately adds or removes that tag for the current selected books without a separate confirmation button.
  • Bulk field actions simplified: collection, availability, and location now sit as stacked dropdown actions with one combined Apply button, replacing separate per-action buttons.
  • Options stayed the control room: tags, collections, locations, CSV export, and PDF export remain together on Options, with tighter dropdown spacing and a cleaner 50/50 export layout.
  • Inventory visibility repaired: the central Auth account ID mismatch that hid the existing wm catalog was fixed so Owner / bootstrap wm access maps back to the current inventory owner.
  • DNS was standardized: the full-name domains were cleaned up for public-network testing, keeping web routes proxied while leaving mail/control-panel records DNS-only and removing an unused localhost record.

This matters because the catalog app is becoming less divided: the daily inventory view, batch tools, export controls, and Auth identity model are settling into their proper places instead of each page carrying a partial duplicate of the others.
